Int.description: Fixed-width machine integer, at least 64-bit. Overflow wraps silently — use Integer when that matters.

Integer.description: Arbitrary-precision integer. Slower than Int but never overflows.

Double.description: IEEE-754 double. `Float` is single precision and rarely worth it.

String.description: `[Char]` — a lazy linked list of characters. Convenient but slow; prefer Text.

Text.description: Packed strict UTF-16 text from the text package.

Bool.description: `False` or `True`, an ordinary data type with no special status.

Maybe.description: `Nothing | Just a` — a total alternative to null.

Either.description: `Left a | Right b`, conventionally error or success.

IO.description: A description of an effectful computation returning a.

list.description: Lazy singly linked list. O(n) index and append; the default sequence type.

tuple.description: Anonymous product, up to 62 components. Fields are lazy.

function.description: A function type. Curried, so `a -> b -> c` is `a -> (b -> c)`.

Map.description: Immutable ordered map with O(log n) operations.

Vector.description: Immutable array with O(1) indexing and fusion.

IORef.description: Mutable reference usable only in IO.

TVar.description: Transactional variable, read and written inside STM.

MVar.description: Full-or-empty mutable box, usable as a mutex.

Constraint.description: The kind of a class constraint, e.g. `Show a`. Enabled by ConstraintKinds.

Type.description: The kind of ordinary lifted types, formerly written `*`.
